questions.question_text: Eliminate the arbitrary function $f$ from $z=f(xy/z)$ and form the partial differential equation.
questions.answer: The relation implies locally that $z$ depends only on $xy$. Thus $p=yh\prime(xy)$, $q=xh\prime(xy)$, and $xp=yq$.
Charpit’s equations imply $q/p=a$ on a nondegenerate branch. Then $p=2/[3\sqrt{z+a^2}]$, so integrating $dz=p(dx+a\,dy)$ gives $(z+a^2)^{3/2}=x+ay+b$. Sign choices give other local branches.

questions.question_text: Find the root mean square value of $f(x)=x^2$ in $(0,\pi)$.
questions.answer: $\sqrt{\pi^{-1}\int_0^\pi x^4dx}=\pi^2/\sqrt5$.

questions.question_text: Write down the initial condition when a taut string of length $2l$ is fastened on both ends. The midpoint of the string is taken to a height $b$ and released from the rest in that position.
questions.answer: $y(x,0)=bx/l$ for $0\le x\le l$, $y(x,0)=b(2l-x)/l$ for $l\le x\le2l$, and $y_t(x,0)=0$. The fixed ends also give $y(0,t)=y(2l,t)=0$.

questions.question_text: Prove that $F[f(ax)]=\frac1aF(s/a)$, $a>0$.
questions.answer: In the Fourier integral put $u=ax$; then $dx=du/a$ and the exponential frequency becomes $s/a$.

questions.question_text: Find the Fourier sine transform of $f(x)=e^{-x}$.
questions.answer: $F_s(s)=\sqrt{2/\pi}\int_0^\infty e^{-x}\sin sx\,dx=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,s/(1+s^2)$.

questions.question_text: Prove that $Z[1/(n+1)]=z\log(z/(z-1))$.
(i) Find the singular integral of $z=px+qy+p^2-q^2$. (ii) Solve $x(y-z)p+y(z-x)q=z(x-y)$.
questions.answer: (i) The envelope of $z=ax+by+a^2-b^2$ is $z=(y^2-x^2)/4$. (ii) The characteristic system has invariants $x+y+z$ and $x^2+y^2+z^2$, so $\Phi(x+y+z,x^2+y^2+z^2)=0$.

questions.question_text: Solve $(D^2-2DD\prime)z=e^{2x}+x^3y$.
questions.answer: Factoring $D(D-2D\prime)$ gives the complementary function $\phi(y)+\psi(y+2x)$. The particular integral is $e^{2x}/4+x^5y/20+x^6/60$, as direct substitution verifies.

questions.question_text: Expand $x(2\pi-x)$ as Fourier series in $(0,2\pi)$. Deduce the sum of $1+1/2^2+1/3^2+\cdots$.
questions.answer: Writing $u=x-\pi$ gives $\pi^2-u^2$, hence $x(2\pi-x)=2\pi^2/3-4\sum_{n\ge1}\cos(nx)/n^2$. At $x=0$ this gives $\sum1/n^2=\pi^2/6$.

questions.question_text: Find the Fourier series upto second harmonics from the following data: $x=0,\pi/3,2\pi/3,\pi,4\pi/3,5\pi/3,2\pi$; $y=1,1.4,1.9,1.7,1.5,1.2,1$.
questions.answer: The discrete coefficients from the six distinct values give $y\approx29/20-(11/30)\cos x+(\sqrt3/10)\sin x-(1/10)\cos2x-(\sqrt3/30)\sin2x$.

questions.question_text: A tightly stretched string with end points $x=0$ and $x=l$ is initially at rest in its equilibrium position. If it is set vibrating giving each point a velocity $\lambda x(l-x)$ find the displacement of the string.
questions.answer: The initial velocity coefficients are $B_n=4\lambda l^2[1-(-1)^n]/(n^3\pi^3)$. For wave speed $c$, $y(x,t)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{B_nl}{n\pi c}\sin(n\pi x/l)\sin(n\pi ct/l)$.

questions.question_text: A rectangular plate with insulated surfaces is 10 cm wide and so long compared to its width that it may be considered as an infinite plate. If the temperature along short edge $y=0$ is $u(x,0)=8\sin(\pi x/l)$, $0<x<10$, while two long edges $x=0$ and $x=10$ as well as the other short edge are kept at 0°, find the steady state temperature at any point of the plate.
questions.answer: If the printed $l$ denotes the width $10$, separation gives $u=8e^{-\pi y/10}\sin(\pi x/10)$. For general $l$, expand the prescribed short-edge function in the sine basis on $(0,10)$ and multiply each mode by $e^{-n\pi y/10}$.

questions.question_text: Find the Fourier transform of $f(x)=a^2-x^2$ for $|x|<a$, $f(x)=0$ for $|x|>a>0$, and show that $\int_0^\infty[(\sin t-t\cos t)/t^3]^2dt=\pi/15$.
questions.answer: $F(s)=4[\sin(as)-as\cos(as)]/s^3$ for the unnormalized convention. Parseval gives $\int_{-a}^a(a^2-x^2)^2dx=16a^5/15=(1/\pi)\int_0^\infty F(s)^2ds$. Substitution $t=as$ yields the stated integral.

questions.question_text: Find the Fourier sine and cosine transforms of $x^{n-1}$. Hence deduce that $1/\sqrt{x}$ is self reciprocal under both transforms. Also find $F[1/\sqrt{|x|}]$.
questions.answer: For $0<n<1$ and $s>0$, $F_s=\sqrt{2/\pi}\Gamma(n)\sin(n\pi/2)s^{-n}$ and $F_c=\sqrt{2/\pi}\Gamma(n)\cos(n\pi/2)s^{-n}$. At $n=1/2$ both equal $s^{-1/2}$. With symmetric full Fourier normalization, the transform of $|x|^{-1/2}$ is $|s|^{-1/2}$, interpreted as an improper integral or distribution.

questions.question_text: (i) Determine the Z-transform of $\sin(n\pi/2)$ and $\cos(n\pi/2)$. (ii) Find $Z^{-1}\{(z^2+z)/(z-1)^3\}$ by long division method.
questions.answer: (i) Geometric sums give $z/(z^2+1)$ and $z^2/(z^2+1)$ respectively, for $|z|>1$. (ii) In powers of $z^{-1}$, $(z^2+z)/(z-1)^3=\sum_{n\ge0}n^2z^{-n}$, so the inverse is $n^2$.
The characteristic roots are $3,4$ and a particular solution is $2^{n-1}$. Applying the initial values to $y_n=A3^n+B4^n+2^{n-1}$ yields $A=-1$, $B=1/2$, so $y_n=2^{n-1}-3^n+4^n/2$.
